gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the long-copy rate next to the headline speed. Makers advertise 3,707–3,900 MB/s from short benchmarks. ASUS's own 30-minute claim for the PA40SU works out to about 1,644 MB/s. PCWorld's 450 GB write on the UGREEN CM642, ChatGPT's 'best for sustained transfers' pick, was slower than a couple of 20Gbps (about 2 GB/s) USB 3.2×2 SSDs, even though the enclosure 'never suffered any thermal related issues'.
standout_why: Compared against owc.com/solutions/express-1m2 (cited), itechguides (cited), soldermag and Tom's Hardware as quoted in ChatGPT's answer. OWC's page has the Mac vs PC split (3,189 vs 3,836 MB/s), so that part is already covered. itechguides gives long-write figures (1,350/1,700 MB/s) only for OWC's ready-made Envoy Ultra SSD, not for any empty enclosure. ChatGPT's own answer gives Tom's 1.4–1.8 GB/s drop as a general caveat. None of them turns ASUS's '2960 GB in 30 minutes' into MB/s. None says that PCWorld's 450 GB write on the CM642 was slower than 20Gbps drives. Soldermag says 'thermal throttling' for OWC and ACASIS with no numbers. ChatGPT and our current page both report the CM642 450 GB test only as 'no thermal trouble'. Rivals have the general idea that long writes fall to cache speed, but not these per-product figures, so it scores 2 rather than 3.
decides: The CM642 stays the pick for long copies, but for a narrower reason: in PCWorld's 450 GB test it finished without the thermal dropout that stopped the UGREEN CM850, not because it holds about 3.8 GB/s. On copies of hundreds of GB, the SSD's speed after its cache fills and the copy tool (PCWorld saw Explorer vs FastCopy differences on the PA40SU) limit speed more than the enclosure's fan does. The table should show three numbers for each enclosure: the maker's peak, the host-specific cap (Apple Silicon or Thunderbolt), and any long-copy figure. The footnote should say that a 'no throttle' long write lands around 1.6–2 GB/s.

findings.label: Maker's sustained-transfer claim converted to an average rate
findings.value: 2,960 GB in 30 minutes = about 1,644 MB/s average
findings.source_title: ASUS Announces ProArt PA40SU USB4 SSD Enclosure (press release, April 21, 2026)
findings.note: Quote: 'In internal ASUS tests, PA40SU transferred up to 2960GB of data continuously over a 30-minute period.' Arithmetic: 2,960,000 MB ÷ 1,800 s = 1,644 MB/s, about 43% of a 3,800 MB/s USB4 peak. The release does not name the SSD or host, and does not say whether this was reads or writes. The fan is described as a 'four-level smart cooling fan'.

findings.label: PCWorld 450 GB write vs 20Gbps drives
findings.value: 450 GB write was 'actually slower than a couple of USB 3.2×2 20Gbps SSDs'; 'never suffered any thermal related issues'
findings.source_title: Ugreen CM642 SSD enclosure review: Fast, roll-your-own USB4 storage (PCWorld, Feb 11, 2025)
findings.note: Test SSD: WD SN850X 8TB. Host: Z790, i5-12400, Windows 11. Controller: ASM2464PD. The same review calls USB 3.2×2 '20Gbps (roughly 2GBps)', so the 450 GB write averaged under about 2 GB/s. The exact rate is shown only in a chart image. The 48 GB copy was 'fastest ever for a USB4 SSD'. The UGREEN CM850 'required removing its silicon sleeve to complete our 450GB write'.
